inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E (year ended 30 Sep 2026, not yet reported) for 'Siemens core' = Siemens group EXCLUDING Siemens Healthineers and Siemens Financial Services. 9M FY26 actual core revenue 42,648 (group 59,688 - SHL 16,846 - SFS 194, Q3 FY26 release segment table) + Q4 FY26E 16,350 (Q4 FY25 core 15,015 x 1.09, the Q3 FY26 core y/y rate). FY2025 actual core revenue 55,169 (78,914 - 23,375 - 370).
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted, Q3 FY2026 (Apr-Jun 2026): net income attributable 2,270 / diluted EPS 2.91 = 780.1m (continuing basis 2,266/2.90 = 781.4m). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the ongoing buyback (2,656 cash 9M FY26) is the mechanism that keeps the count flat and is value-neutral here.
inputs.net_debt_note: CORE net debt, not total_debt - cash. Industrial net debt 9,342 at 30 Jun 2026 (Q3 FY26 release; Siemens definition: excludes SFS debt, includes pensions 681 and lease liabilities) LESS Siemens Healthineers' own net debt, ESTIMATED at ~11,000. Reason: SHL's debt is largely intra-group loans from Siemens (eliminated on consolidation), so consolidated industrial net debt carries the external debt Siemens raised to fund Varian while SHL's market cap already deducts SHL's full debt. Valuing the SHL stake at market therefore requires removing SHL's whole net debt from the Siemens-core bridge. The 11,000 is NOT in the local filings (SHL's own Q3 FY26 statement is not extracted): replace it with SHL's reported net debt at the next update. Sensitivity: each EUR 1bn = EUR 1.28/share.
inputs.debt_cash_note: Consolidated memo only (short-term 8,600 + long-term 41,324; cash 10,930, 30 Jun 2026). Includes SFS's funding and SHL's external debt, so total_debt - cash is NOT the bridge figure; net_debt above is.
inputs.last_fcf_note: GROUP-level audit trail, FY2025: reported FCF continuing ops 11,004 (Q4 FY25 release) - SBC ~530 (estimate: FY2024 annual note 26 gives 524 incl. 126 Healthineers; FY2025 annual not extracted) - interest income 2,765 (FY25, mostly SFS) = 7,709. This includes Healthineers and SFS and is NOT the projection base. The projections are a component build on Siemens core (ex-SHL, ex-SFS); year-1 (FY2027) core owner FCF is ~6.1bn, ~9.8% of revenue.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2024 Annual Report note 26: equity-settled share-based payment expense, continuing ops, EUR 524m FY24 / 438m FY23, of which Siemens Healthineers plans 126m / 109m. Core (ex-SHL) FY24 = 398m = 0.75% of core revenue 53,154; projected at 0.75% of core revenue. Awards are settled from treasury shares (no net-share-settlement withholding line is disclosed), so equity-award taxes are not separately added. FY2025/FY2026 SBC not in the extracted filings; core_metrics carries no SBC column for any period.
inputs.buyback_note: Purchase of treasury shares: FY2025 2,269; 9M FY2026 2,656 (new programme launched FY26). Siemens is an active repurchaser, so the flat count is funded.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:37:40Z (Xetra regular session, last trade before the weekend)
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built: 10y Bund ~2.7%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.05 -> cost of equity ~8.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (A+ rated issuer) -> 2.6% after 26% tax; core is near net-cash so weight on debt is small -> WACC 7.5%. Same WACC in all scenarios: risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities (~3.2bn group) sit inside Siemens' industrial net debt; lease principal (~0.8bn/yr group, ~0.6bn core) is NOT in EBITDA, so ongoing right-of-use renewal is charged through capex: capex path = ~2.7% PP&E/intangibles (FY24 core 1,367 = 2.6%; FY25 ~3.0%) + ~1.0% ROU renewal = 3.7%. D&A includes ROU depreciation and PPA amortisation (core FY25 1,953 = 3.5%; 9M FY26 3.8%).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once. Healthineers' 33% minority disappears with SHL from the flows (the stake is added at market, 67% only). Remaining minorities (Siemens Ltd India, Siemens Energy India, others; ~EUR 255m/yr NCI profit = 9M FY26 NCI 713 less ~520 Healthineers share, annualised) are deducted in the equity bridge at ~18x, the base terminal cap.
inputs.healthineers_treatment: Siemens Healthineers (SHL.DE) is deconsolidated from the flows: its revenue, EBITDA, D&A, capex, SBC and tax are removed and the 67% stake (Siemens 'subsequently holds 67%', H1 FY26 report note 2) is added to the equity bridge at market value: 1,128m SHL shares x 67% = 755.8m shares x EUR 41.86 (Yahoo SHL.DE, 2026-10-23T15:35Z) = EUR 31,636m = EUR 40.6/share. Rationale: SHL is separately listed with a deep market price; the Nov-2025 plan spins it off to Siemens shareholders (tax rulings received per Q3 FY26 release; AGM vote Feb 2027), which is a value-neutral distribution in kind. After the spin-off the Siemens price will drop by the distributed SHL value and this bridge item must shrink to the retained stake.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with a sum-of-parts bridge. Routing: diversified industrial operating company (automation, electrification, rail) -> owner-FCF + non-US/cyclical adaptations (EUR WACC, lease treatment A, NCI once, matching-asset rule). Embedded lender (SFS) and listed stakes (Healthineers, Siemens Energy) valued separately and summed, per the straddle rule in dcf-methods. First valuation of SIE.DE (no MEMORY entry). Flows = Siemens core = DI + SI + Mobility + reconciliation items (corporate, innovation, real estate, eliminations), excluding SHL and SFS. Core EBITDA FY26E: segments 9M 7,448 + Q4E ~2,800 + normalised reconciliation ~+250 (FY24 +634, FY25 -100, 9M FY26 +755 incl. a 227 Fluence gain) = ~10,500 = 17.8% reported; ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC (reported + 0.75pp SBC) because the engine deducts SBC separately. Financial income (interest on cash, SFS interest, SE dividends) is outside EBITDA, so no interest is in the projected flows and none needs stripping; its source assets are in the bridge. Cash tax 26% of EBIT (group ETR ~25%; cash taxes 2.65bn FY25 group). Working capital: manufacturer, receivables + contract assets + inventory (38.6bn) exceed payables + contract liabilities (23.4bn), so growth consumes cash -> wc_capture negative (-10%), partly offset by Mobility/SI customer prepayments on a 1.23 book-to-bill. Post-2020 (post Energy spin-off) history only is used for the trend. Healthineers' SHL net debt (11,000) and the Q4 FY26 cash item are estimates to be replaced by the FY2026 annual (due mid-Nov 2026).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025, post Siemens Energy spin-off), used as a cross-check only; the forward path is built from FY26 guidance and backlog, not from a CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.3% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 6.7%: equity is inflated by fair-value gains on the Siemens Energy stake through OCI (+4.5bn in 9M FY25, +3.1bn in 9M FY26) and by Healthineers stake sales booked directly in equity, so it overstates operating compounding. EPS CAGRs are distorted by the FY2022 Siemens Energy write-down (EPS 4.59) and the FY2025 Innomotics disposal gain (2.62/share discontinued).
historical_growth.notes: Group consolidated figures, FY2020-FY2025, from Metrics.csv. Owner-FCF CAGRs are FCF less interest income (FY20 1,547, FY22 1,632, FY25 2,765); SBC could NOT be deducted across the history because it is disclosed only for FY23 (438) and FY24 (524) in the extracted filings. The owner-FCF CAGR (7.6% 3yr) is below reported (10.1%) because interest income on cash/SFS grew faster than operating cash flow as rates rose. Healthineers is inside all of these group figures.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 6.5%: 9M FY26 book-to-bill 1.23 and record backlog (EUR 132bn group), SI guided 10-11% comp, DI recovering 7-10%, Mobility 5-7%, minus ~1pp FX. Decelerates to 3% nominal by FY33 as the electrification/data-centre cycle normalises.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA. FY26E core 17.8% reported = 18.55% pre-SBC. FY27 held at 18.5% because the Sept-2026 >6,000 job cuts (mostly automation) bring severance; then +1pp to 19.5% from software mix (Altair/Dotmatics, EDA), SI pricing and the cost programme. Equals ~18.75% reported, below FY23's peak-cycle DI-led level.

scenario_narratives.base: Electrification and data-centre power demand keep Smart Infrastructure growing high-single to double digits for two to three years, Digital Industries completes its recovery from the FY24-25 destocking downturn but faces Chinese competition (Inovance) in factory automation, and Mobility converts its backlog at 8-10% margins. Core revenue grows 6.5% in FY27 fading to 3%; the automation job cuts cost a year of margin and then lift core pre-SBC EBITDA to 19.5% with the software mix from Altair/Dotmatics. Healthineers is spun off at roughly today's market value.
scenario_narratives.bull: The data-centre/grid build-out proves a multi-year super-cycle (Q3 FY26 SI orders +40%), DI's software and industrial-AI push (Nvidia 'Industrial AI Operating System', Siemens Industrial Copilot, SaaS transition) lifts growth and mix, and the cost programme sticks: core grows 8.5% for two years and margins reach 21% pre-SBC, the kind of focused, higher-growth 'core' the post-spin re-rating thesis needs. Terminal cap 20x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Factory automation proves structurally impaired: Chinese low-cost rivals take share, European manufacturing stays weak, the data-centre order wave pauses after FY26's surge and a stronger euro (net exporter) cuts nominal growth. Core revenue is flat in FY28, margins fall to ~16.75% as volumes drop through restructuring, Mobility hits a fixed-price project overrun, and Altair/Dotmatics integration under-delivers. Recovery to only 17.5% pre-SBC and 2.5% growth; terminal cap 15x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default because Digital Industries' automation business is short-cycle and under structural Chinese pressure (Sept-2026 cuts of >6,000 jobs) and FY26 orders are at a cyclical high. Base 50% as the guided, backlog-supported path. Bull cut to 25% because it needs the electrification super-cycle, the automation recovery and a software-led margin step-up to all land together. No balance-sheet or refinancing risk motivates the bear weight - the core is near net cash.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Siemens is valued as the sum of a core industrial (DI, SI, Mobility, corporate) on an owner-FCF basis plus its listed stakes at market and its captive lender at a multiple of earnings. The core flows exclude Healthineers entirely; the 67% SHL stake enters the bridge at market value together with an adjustment that removes SHL's net debt (mostly owed to Siemens) from consolidated industrial net debt. This makes the valuation invariant to the pending spin-off: distributing SHL shares moves value from the Siemens line to the shareholder's SHL holding without changing the total.
key_risks_to_valuation: SHL net debt estimate (EUR 11.0bn) is not from a local filing; +/- EUR 1bn = -/+ EUR 1.28/share
Healthineers stake is marked to SHL.DE's market price; a 10% move in SHL = EUR 4.1/share
Factory-automation cyclicality and Chinese competition in Digital Industries (bear axis)
Terminal cap binds in base and bull: value is sensitive to the exit multiple chosen for a cyclical industrial
Q4 FY2026 cash item (EUR 3.5bn) is an estimate pending the FY2026 annual results
SBC for FY25/FY26 not in the extracted filings; 0.75% of core revenue is extrapolated from FY24
